scannedAt: derived from the build; see the run that produced it

categories.title: Draft or sample event records in production output
categories.detail: A review fixture reaching a production build would present an illustrative session as an announcement.

categories.title: Review watermark copy in production output
categories.detail: The illustrative label belongs only to a review build. In production it would either be a lie about real content, or evidence that fixtures shipped.

categories.title: Participant email values
categories.detail: Only the non-deliverable placeholder you@example.com is permitted, and only as form placeholder copy.

categories.title: Unapproved statistic, capacity, attendance or urgency claim
categories.detail: A seat count, an attendance figure or an urgency phrase would each be a fact PAAIPE has not supplied.

categories.title: Dead links and controls that pretend to work
categories.detail: An href="#" or a disabled-looking control that is keyboard-active invites an action the site cannot complete.

categories.title: Draft legal copy exposed as final
categories.detail: A policy still awaiting review must say so on the page. A draft presented as in force is the failure mode with legal consequences.

categories.title: An analytics vendor in the build
categories.detail: This portal ships no analytics. A vendor script in an artifact would be telemetry nobody consented to.

categories.title: A forbidden telemetry key in the build
categories.detail: Matched as a payload KEY rather than a bare word: this site legitimately says "email" in its privacy notice, its FAQ and its form label, and a guard nobody can keep green is a guard that gets deleted.

categories.title: A production mock that reports registration success
categories.detail: No build may contain a code path that announces a completed registration without a confirmed gateway response.
